identificationModule.briefTitle: Outcome of Acquired Haemophilia With Steroid Combined With Cyclophosphamide Versus Steroid Combined With Rituximab (CREHA Study)
identificationModule.officialTitle: Outcome of Acquired Haemophilia With Steroid Combined With Cyclophosphamide Versus Steroid Combined With Rituximab (CREHA Study)

descriptionModule.briefSummary: CREHA project is a study comparing steroid combined with cyclophosphamide versus steroid combined with rituximab in patients with acquired haemophilia. The study will test the hypothesis that steroid combined with cyclophosphamide is more effective than steroid plus rituximab for FVIII inhibitor eradication in acquired haemophilia.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: CREHA project is a multicenter, randomized, controlled efficacity and safety study comparing steroid combined with cyclophosphamide versus steroid combined with rituximab in patients with acquired haemophilia. The study will test the hypothesis that steroid combined with cyclophosphamide is more effective than steroid plus rituximab for FVIII inhibitor eradication in acquired haemophilia

armGroups.label: Bras B
armGroups.description: Steroid 1mg/kg/d and Rituximab 375 mg/m2 every week during four weeks

primaryOutcomes.description: Demonstrate the inferiority of steroid combined with rituximab as compared to the recommended immunosuppressive approach (steroid combined with cysclophosphamide for 21 to 42 days) as the first-line immunosuppressive therapy for FVIII inhibitor eradication in acquired haemophilia
The primary efficacy outcome is the proportion of patients achieving complete remission defined as titer FVII inhibitor lower than 0.4 Bethesda unit and factor VIII level \> 50%
The primary safety outcomes will be the occurrence of major bleeding and infection related immunosuppressive treatment adverse events.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Secondary objective are time to complete remission, number of relapse at M6, M12, M18, adverse events (especially related to bleeding or to immunosuppressive treatment) and mortality
The other key safety outcome are clinically relevant non major bleeding, diabetes and mortality non-related with acquired haemophilia or immunosuppressive therapy

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* men or women
* women post-menpausal or with ongoing contraception
* 18 years old or more
* diagnosis of acquired hemophilia
* patient must be insured
* patient has provided written informed consent prior to enrolment
* patient compliant

Exclusion Criteria:

* constitutional hemophilia
* chemotherapy
* ongoing treatment with prednisone \> 20mg further more 1 month
* ongoing treatment with prednisone \>0.7 mg/d further more 10 days
* thrombocytopenia
* leukopenia
* chronic disease
